title: Ignored error in ReadinessHandler JSON encoding
description: The json.NewEncoder(w).Encode() call can fail but the error is ignored with //nolint:errcheck. Any encoding error will leave the response incomplete and the client will receive invalid data. The nolint directive suppresses legitimate linter warnings.
recommended_action: Check the error: if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(...); err != nil { http.Error(w, "internal server error", http.StatusInternalServerError); return }

title: http.Error after partial write in OrdersHandler has no effect
description: Calling http.Error() after json.NewEncoder.Encode() has already started writing to the ResponseWriter will not change the already-sent HTTP status code. The error handling is cosmetically present but functionally ineffective for the client.
recommended_action: Encode to a buffer first: b, err := json.Marshal(orders); if err != nil { http.Error(...) return }; w.Write(b)

title: Invalid Go version in go.mod
description: Go 1.27.0 does not exist. Go version numbers are currently in the 1.21–1.22 range. Specifying a non-existent version causes toolchain compatibility issues and indicates outdated or incorrect module metadata.
recommended_action: Change to a real released version such as 'go 1.22' or 'go 1.21'

title: Missing explicit WriteHeader(200) before body write in OrdersHandler
evidence:
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(orders); err != nil {
description: The handler sets Content-Type but never explicitly calls WriteHeader(http.StatusOK). Relying on implicit 200 is fragile; explicit is more maintainable.
recommended_action: Add w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) after setting headers and before writing the body

title: Missing explicit WriteHeader(200) in ReadinessHandler
description: Same as CQ-004: implicit 200 OK. Explicit WriteHeader is a best practice.

title: DB_DSN environment variable read but never used
description: DB_DSN is parsed and defaulted but the value is never passed to any downstream component (no database connection is opened). This creates confusion about what dependencies the app actually has.
recommended_action: Either remove the DB_DSN block or connect it to an actual database client initialization

title: LOG_LEVEL read but logging does not respect it
description: LOG_LEVEL is read and printed but the standard log package used throughout the app does not support level filtering. The configuration has no functional effect.
recommended_action: Either replace the standard log package with a leveled logger (e.g., slog) that respects LOG_LEVEL, or remove the variable

title: Inconsistent lowercase HTTP error message text
description: Error message uses lowercase text. Standard practice is to use http.StatusText() which returns canonically capitalised strings, keeping error responses consistent across the API.

title: Inconsistent lowercase HTTP error message in ReadinessHandler
description: Same as CQ-008: lowercase error text.

title: HTTP server timeouts are hardcoded constants
evidence:
ReadTimeout:  10 * time.Second,
WriteTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
IdleTimeout:  60 * time.Second,
description: Timeout values are not configurable. Different environments (dev vs prod) may need different tuning without code changes.
recommended_action: Expose READ_TIMEOUT_SEC, WRITE_TIMEOUT_SEC, IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC environment variables with the current values as defaults

title: Shutdown grace period is hardcoded
description: The 30-second shutdown grace period is not configurable. Long-running requests in production may need a different timeout.
recommended_action: Make configurable via SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SEC environment variable with 30s default

title: log.Fatalf in goroutine bypasses graceful shutdown
description: Calling log.Fatalf() inside a goroutine will call os.Exit(1) immediately, bypassing the defer cancel() and the graceful shutdown channel logic. In-flight requests will be terminated abruptly.
recommended_action: Use an error channel: errCh := make(chan error, 1); go func() { if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != http.ErrServerClosed { errCh <- err } }(); then select on errCh and quit channel

title: Request context not propagated to downstream operations
description: Handlers do not use r.Context(). When database or external calls are added later, cancellation and deadline propagation will need to be retrofitted.
recommended_action: Establish the pattern now: pass r.Context() to any downstream calls as they are added

title: Inconsistent log format across main.go
evidence: log.Printf("level=%s msg=\"server starting\" addr=:%s", logLevel, port)
description: Line 49 uses key=value structured logging while other log lines use plain string messages. Inconsistency makes log aggregation and parsing unreliable.
recommended_action: Adopt a single log format throughout, preferably structured (key=value or JSON)

title: PORT environment variable accepted without validation
description: An invalid PORT value (non-numeric, out of range 1–65535) will cause srv.ListenAndServe() to fail with a non-obvious error at runtime rather than at startup with a clear configuration error.
recommended_action: Validate the port value: parse as integer, check range 1–65535, and exit early with a descriptive error if invalid
